headline: Creative midfielder and set-piece threat, developed as an attacking midfielder at the Real Salt Lake Academy. Four-time All-WAC at Utah Valley, a program record.
quote: On the other side of fear is what you wanna be, but it's just disguised as fear.

1st Team All-WAC · team leader in assists

p: Alejandro Silva was born and raised in Salt Lake City, the son of Elsa and José Luis Silva and one of four brothers. He learned the game in the city's Hispanic Sunday leagues, with his dad as his first teacher, and played club soccer for La Roca, winning a 2018 Utah Youth Soccer Association state title.

He came up through the Real Salt Lake Academy as an attacking midfielder for the U-19 team. When the academy first offered him a spot, he admits he was scared to take it. He took it anyway. He trained with the Real Monarchs and started in their preseason, then heard the words every academy player fears: they would not sign him.

He turned that rejection into one of the best careers in Utah Valley history. He started every match he played across four seasons (56 starts), earned All-WAC honours a program-record four times, including First Team in 2022 and 2023, and became the 11th player in program history to pass 4,000 minutes. As a senior he led the team in goals, and his strike against Pacific was named WAC Top Play.

He finished his college career as a graduate transfer at Oregon State. It was a step up, and also, in his words, one of the lowest moments of his career. He talks openly about reaching out for help, and about the person who helped him through it.

Since college he has kept playing, including a spell with Utah United. He describes life after college as harder than college itself, because the system that structured every day is gone, and he is still chasing the professional game.

quotes: People only see the glory, but there's so much more behind the scenes that's not seen.
It's only you who can decide if you're gonna make it or not.

card_line: Southampton FC Academy · Utah Valley University
quote: I know it's not gonna be easy. But I'm not gonna stop here.

p: Gilles Aurelien grew up in Bracknell, England, with a football at his feet and a father who believed in him before anyone else did. At seven, a scout invited him to trial at Southampton FC. He spent eight-plus years in the academy, traveling across Europe and winning Player of the Tournament in Spain.

COVID wiped out his post-academy trials. He and his dad chose America. He started at Otero Junior College, helped the program reach nationals for the first time in 12 years, then tore his ACL nine games into his sophomore season. His father flew from the UK for the surgery.
He came back. He transferred to Utah Valley University, became one of the best midfielders in the WAC, and graduated with a BS degree.
After graduating, he returned to pursue professional opportunities. He was listed for the MLS SuperDraft. He has played against pros. He is not done.

card_line: Right to Dream · Salt Lake CC · Lindsey Wilson
headline: Quick, confident winger developed at Right to Dream Academy, with European club experience. Now a junior at Lindsey Wilson University.
quote: Don't give up on your dream, and make right choices and smart decision.
as_of: Updated November 2, 2026. Lindsey Wilson stats through October 29, 2026.

p: Bony Ulrich grew up in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire. His mother wanted him in school, so he snuck out to play. Some mornings he woke up at 4:30 and walked an hour to practice with the other boys, waking each other up and hopping trucks to get there.

At nine, he showed up to a trial with dyed hair so he would stand out among more than a hundred kids. It worked. He was picked for Right to Dream, the academy in Ghana, and left home to chase the game. In his words, the hardest part of moving to Ghana was the food.

sections.h: Europe, and the clubs that said no
p: Right to Dream took him to FC Nordsjælland in Denmark and to tournaments and trials across Europe. Over the years he has played in more than 25 countries. Teammates he started with went on to play professionally at the top level, while trial after trial ended with a version of the same answer: they wanted bigger players. A bad experience with an agent cost him a contract.

During COVID, caught between Spain and Norway and told to go back to Ghana, he came close to quitting. Along the way, a mentor, a Ghanaian professional player who later passed away on the field, talked him out of giving up on the game.

He rebuilt his career in the United States at Salt Lake Community College and moved on to Lindsey Wilson University, where he is a junior in 2026. Off the pitch he describes himself as shy. On it, he says, he is different. His long-term goal is to become an agent himself, so young players get the guidance he didn't.

quotes: Outside the field, I'm a shy person though. But on the field, nah, I'm different.
I just wanna be an agent.

card_line: Toronto FC Academy · Snow College · Utah United
quote: Your ceiling is someone else's floor. Keep climbing.

p: Elijah Tenger was born in Nigeria, where football is not a hobby, it is life. From four years old, his father was his first coach. At twelve, his family immigrated to Canada.
He earned a spot at Toronto FC Academy at U14, continued at the De Rosario Academy from U16 to U18, and trained at Phoenix Football Academy in Abuja.
COVID nearly closed the window. When it reopened, he earned a spot among the top sixty players across Canada.
In 2024 he trained with Real Monarchs of MLS Next Pro, won Player of the Year in the UPSL Mountain Division, and made the USL Academy All-Tournament Team. He was top scorer again in 2025.
He is the first person in his family to go to college, and he is still chasing a professional contract.

quote: I left everything I knew. But I never left my dream.

stats.l: SLCC record: SWAC and Region 18 champions

p: Sharif Sayawu grew up in Agona Duakwa, a small town in Ghana where football is not something you choose, it is something that chooses you. His parents, Iddrisu Sayawu and Ayishatu Mohammed, believed in what they saw and sacrificed to make sure he had the chance to pursue it.

He earned his way to Phoenix Academy, one of Ghana's most respected development programs, which has sent players to MLS, USL, and NCAA Division I. He repaid their belief with 15 goals in 2023 and Best Player honors at the 2024 Showcase. The calls from America came. He chose Utah Valley University.

Getting on that plane was one of the hardest things he has ever done. He left his family, his country, and everything familiar, and arrived in Utah as a freshman. In his very first collegiate game he recorded two assists. Weeks later he scored his first Division I goal.

After a season at Utah Valley, Sharif transferred to Salt Lake Community College, where he is a sophomore forward in 2026. He is still carrying the hopes of a family back in Ghana, and his story is just beginning.
